## session: product-docs Ext 2 — 7 cross-cutting capability docs prod-docs-ext2 — 2026-04-17

**Purpose:** Drafted 7 cross-cutting capability docs (E1–E7) for `frontend/docs/product/`, expanding the product-docs set from 27 → 34. Each includes a dedicated Improvement opportunities subsection (~17 items/doc, ~120 total). Final set: Jobs 7 + User 7 + Admin 7 + System 13.

**Insights:**

1. **Verify agent claims against the cited line before embedding them in canonical docs.** The E6 Stripe agent asserted a WHERE-clause bug at `src/db/methods/stripe.db.ts:84`; direct read showed the param was destructured-and-renamed (`{ id: stripeSessionId }`) and the column reference was correct. If the bug had been included, engineers treating the doc as ground truth would have chased a phantom. Pattern: research agents read partial code and hallucinate bugs; spot-check every structural claim, not just the content.
2. **Companion-doc drift is a first-class output of system docs.** Three of seven Ext 2 docs ended up flagging stale claims in their sibling user-\* docs: `user-buy-credits.md` asserts a Stripe webhook that doesn't exist; `user-templates.md:76` claims upload templates are hidden by default (code hides only download + validation); `.claude/rules/server-actions.md` claims localStorage persistence but `app-wrapper.client.tsx` uses plain `QueryClientProvider`. Treat drift-flagging as a deliverable, not a side-effect — surface it in Improvement opportunities with file:line citations rather than silently aligning.
3. **Polymorphic framing collapses "add a new type" into a small migration.** E7 reframed the four template types as "one engine, four projections" via the `templateType` enum + typed `config` jsonb discriminator. This made the scraper-template gap (improvement #1) feel like a small enum addition rather than speculative new-feature work. Reusable pattern whenever a schema uses a discriminator + union config.
4. **Heading drift is cheap to catch and cheap to fix.** A simple `grep -n "^## "` sweep across all 7 docs caught one drift (E7's "Feature flow" vs canonical "Submission flow") and one benign naming split (E1–E5 "Who uses this doc" vs E6–E7 + original 27 "Who uses it"). Structural grep pass before content review is a cheap quality gate.
5. **Intentional "See also" inversion:** docs about data infrastructure (E3 data-fetching, E4 DB stack) point their See-also at code files rather than sibling docs, with sibling-doc links in Ecosystem instead. This is a useful variation worth preserving — an engineer debugging the query layer needs `src/utils/hooks/use-q.ts`, not another markdown file. Structural validators should accept this variant.
6. **Append-only log chronology matters.** The session started treating the RUNTIME-EXT2.md Section 8 log as "newest-at-top" (matching runtime-notes convention) but Section 8 is append-bottom chronological. Two entries had to be re-ordered. Rule: check the existing order of the target log before prepending vs appending; they're not all the same.

## core-dump: E2E test infrastructure split + middleware fix — 2026-04-16

**Purpose:** Checkpoint the session that split page-modules.spec.ts into  
 test/lib/, added a sentinel video test, and fixed the /api/e2e-test 401 caused

 proxy.ts middleware.

**Insights:**

1. proxy.ts intercepts ALL /api/\* routes before route handlers run — any route  
   using non-session auth (shared secret, API key) must be added to a selfAuthPaths
   bypass list. Symptom: 401 with zero server-side logs.
2. Next.js treats \_ prefixed route folder segments as private/ignored — \_test,  
   \_api etc. will not register as routes. Use plain names (e2e-test not \_test).

   named sentinel test at the end of the describe block to make this deterministic
   regardless of which real tests are enabled.
4. video.path() must be called AFTER browserCtx.close() — the .webm file is only
   finalized on context close; calling before close returns a path to an incomplete
   file.
5. test.use({ viewport }) does not apply to manually created BrowserContext —  
   must set viewport directly in browser.newContext().

   contains HTML attribute values. href="#", id="#something", hash URLs all contain
   "# which prematurely terminates r#"..."#. A rule: if the string will embed HTML,
   use r##.
3. **SVG interactivity pattern**: Wrap rect+text pairs in <g data-svgid="...">  
   with pointer-events: none on child text. Click/hover handlers on the group  
   cleanly fire once per node regardless of which child the cursor hits.
4. **Language metadata at collection time**: When a file-type-aware feature  
   (syntax highlighting) depends on metadata, thread the metadata from the data  
   source (collect_config_files) through the data model (Snapshot.config_files) to
   the renderer — don't infer it from human-readable titles at render time.
5. format!()** + large JS blocks**: Extract JS into a let svg_js = r##"..."##  
   variable before the format!() call. Avoids {{/}} escaping noise in the format  
   string and makes the JS readable.

## core-dump: fix-zsh-4e — zsh banner + Claude PATH — 2026-04-11

**Purpose:** Diagnose and fix zsh banner blocking terminal init + Claude Bash tool "command not found" failures.

**Insights:**

1. Claude Code's Bash tool uses `zsh -f -c "eval 'cmd'"` — fast mode, ALL rc files bypassed including `.zshenv`. The ONLY reliable way to inject PATH or env vars for the Bash tool is via `settings.json` `env` section.
2. Stale-while-revalidate banner pattern: `[ -f cache ] && /bin/cat cache; (script > cache &)` gives instant startup from cache; async refresh for next time. Use `/bin/cat` explicitly when `cat` is aliased to `glow`.
3. `/usr/libexec/path_helper -s` (eval'd) is the correct macOS way to reconstruct system PATH from `/etc/paths` and `/etc/paths.d/`; safe to call from `.zshenv` as a defensive layer even if `-f` mode bypasses it.
4. When diagnosing broken PATH with broken PATH: use `/usr/bin/python3` (absolute) with `os.environ` and `repr()` to get the exact bytes; side-steps all shell PATH lookup issues.
5. Core-dump cannot call `lock-file.sh` when PATH is broken — the script uses `dirname` (needs `/usr/bin`). Skip lock in extremis; document the skip.

## session: feature-docs multi-pass doc generation docs-feat-d1 — 2026-04-14

**Purpose:** Autonomous generation of comprehensive docs for (1) Scraper Success
Modal Flow and (2) Admin Parts List table, using a 7-stage per-feature iteration
(scan → meta → structure → v1 → notes → v2 → notes → v3).

**Insights:**

1. **Single-doc mixed audience beats split files.** Rather than producing  
   separate Notion (ops) and GitHub (eng) versions, the final v3 drafts use one  
   file with "Read this if you..." entry-point callouts, italic customer-quote  
   prefixes for ops sections, and code blocks for eng sections. Half the authoring
   cost, and cross-references stay stable.
2. **Promote limitations with **[CRITICAL]** markers, not just section ordering.
   ** In Scraper v3 §9, promoting non-atomic multi-mutation (§9.1) and  
   DefaultCycleUUID sentinel (§9.3) with [CRITICAL] prefixes made them visually  
   jump out during skim — more effective than bold headers because the marker  
   survives Notion/GitHub paste.
3. **Investigate handwaves before v2, not v3.** The DefaultCycleUUID  
   classification ("is this a bug or intentional?") sat as a v1 handwave. Grepping
   default.db.ts:6 before drafting v2 let it be upgraded to "deliberate sentinel  
   with documented downside" in v2 instead of v3, saving a whole review cycle.
4. **v1→v2 is structural, v2→v3 is polish.** v1 reviews identified 10 priorities
   each (section-level rewrites). v2 reviews identified 13–14 priorities each but  
   nearly all were one-line fixes (move callout to top, add closing sentence,  
   standardize phrasing). Budgeting accordingly prevents over-engineering v2 and  
   under-engineering v3.
5. **Cross-doc standardization requires explicit checklist entries.** K43  
   delimiter phrasing and file-path cross-links between Scraper §9.6 ↔ Parts List  
   §12.4 only stayed consistent because the v2 review notes for _both_ docs  
   explicitly listed "standardize with other doc" as a priority. Leaving it  
   implicit = drift.
6. **ASCII over mermaid for mixed GitHub/Notion.** Mermaid renders natively on  
   GitHub but appears as code in Notion. ASCII diagrams using box-drawing  
   characters render as monospace on both — universally readable is worth the small
   drop in fidelity.

   differentiation via bg-muted/20 or bg-card to avoid blinding white voids in  
   light mode — on dark backgrounds the same void reads as subtle; on white it

5. For multi-column forecast layouts, slice approach `col_a, col_b = fc[0:4], fc[4:8]` + `for j in range(4)` is cleaner and avoids off-by-one bugs from `range(0, N, step)` iteration

## core-dump: audit-start-7a startup optimization — 2026-04-10

**Purpose:** Full checkpoint of Ghostty + Claude Code startup optimization session. 3-phase work: audit, MCP cleanup, shell/statusline fixes.

**Insights:**

1. NVM `--no-use` flag is the single biggest shell startup win (~400ms / 64% of total) — eliminates `nvm_auto` without losing on-demand version switching. Always prefer this over lazy-load patterns.
2. `date +%s` consolidation in daemon loops: 9 calls → 1 saved ~40ms/cycle. Any idempotent-per-iteration subprocess call should be hoisted to loop top.
3. Complexity delta (2x `find` + `wc -l`) was running every 4s but only changes when code is edited — 30s cadence via timestamp file is the right pattern for expensive background operations.
4. Claude Code bash sandbox has persistent issues with basic commands (grep, echo, cat, cp returning exit 127) when user has shell aliases like `alias cat="glow"` or `alias grep="grep --color=auto"`. Workaround: use Read/Write/Grep tools, or explicit paths like `/bin/cp`.
5. MCP server version pinning: unpinned `npx -y` hits npm registry on every startup (200-500ms per server). Pinning eliminated this for 4 servers.
6. Always create \_bak files before editing shell configs — a failed zshrc can lock the user out of their terminal.

## core-dump: statusline v4 fix session stat-fix-2e — 2026-04-08 17:48

**Purpose:** Fix 4 bugs discovered after v4 rendering rewrite: dead v3 code, git
cache format, bash 3.2 empty arrays, \_vlen subshell.

**Insights:**

1. macOS bash 3.2 (GPL v2) crashes with set -u on empty arrays arr=() when  
   accessed as "${arr[@]}". Fix: "${arr[@]-}" — one extra char, no restructuring.
2. printf '%s %s' "" "0" writes " 0". read -r a b skips leading whitespace so  
   a="0" and b="" — values swap silently. Use newlines as delimiters.
3. cp commands went to background silently in this environment. install -m 755  
   is a reliable workaround when cp misbehaves.
4. When inserting a large block of new code in place of old code, verify the old
   code was actually removed (check line counts / search for old markers). "Insert
   but forget to delete" leaves both versions executing.
5. \_vlen() was using echo "${#s}" which spawns a subshell on every call. Changed
  to _VLEN="${#s}" global var pattern — zero subshell forks in loops.

## session: Statusline improvements — MCP fix, overflow, adaptive, research, interactive UX impro-stat-7a — 2026-04-07

**Purpose:** Fix 5 statusline issues: MCP-down spam, multi-line overflow, adaptive scaling, external reference research, interactive customization UX.

**Insights:**

1. Stdio MCP servers (npx/uvx) are spawned on-demand by Claude Code — `pgrep -f` is fundamentally unreliable for detecting them. Distinguish managed vs persistent servers; trust managed ones when parent process is alive.
2. Budget-based overflow prevention (predict line count, trim lowest-priority segments) is cleaner than fixed limits. Use `_count_lines()` before rendering to decide what fits.
3. Bash 3.2 on macOS lacks negative array indexing (`unset 'arr[-1]'` silently fails). Use `arr=("${arr[@]:0:N}")` slicing instead.
4. Session phase detection (early/active/deep based on turn count) combined with tightened auto-thresholds dramatically reduces noise in early sessions.
5. The playground's 3-layer architecture (client preview + server real render + config sync) provides instant feedback while keeping accuracy. Mock data sliders let users simulate session states they haven't reached yet.
6. ccstatusline's most adoptable patterns: flex separators for right-alignment, fish-style path abbreviation, hide-when-empty semantics, and CustomCommand widget for extensibility. Dan's script shows `jq '... // empty'` is critical to avoid "null" string corruption.

## create-report: PDF print CSS for notion, data-table, minimal impr-print-a3 —

2026-  
 04-07

**Purpose:** Added comprehensive @media print styles to three templates so  
 Chrome print-to-PDF produces clean, readable, white-background output.

**Insights:**

1. CSS details[open] cannot be toggled via @media print rules — the open  
   attribute is an HTML attribute, not a CSS property. Use JS  
   beforeprint/afterprint events in shared.js to force tree <details> open during  
   print and restore after.
2. Each style template needs its own @media print block that forces light-mode  
   CSS variable overrides (e.g., --bg: #ffffff, --text: dark-color) — the shared-  
   base.css print rules handle layout/pagination but cannot override style-specific
   variables.
3. data-table's tabbed layout hides non-active .tab-panel elements. Print CSS  
   must force display: block !important on ALL tab panels so the PDF includes every
   section, not just the currently active tab.
4. Playwright's page.pdf() respects emulateMedia() overrides — calling  
   emulateMedia({ media: 'screen' }) before PDF generation defeats @media print  
   rules. Use emulateMedia({ media: null }) to reset before page.pdf().
5. shared-base.css print block handles universal concerns: @page margins, hiding
   interactive UI (theme-toggle, width-picker, search, dialogs, buttons), code pre-
   wrap, table header repeat, heading break-after: avoid, and link URL display via
   ::after pseudo-element.
6. Remaining 10 styles (default, dashboard, magazine, terminal, feed, corporate,
   academic, neon, jupyter, slide) still need print CSS — the pattern established  
   here (force light variables + hide style-specific UI) can be replicated.

## session: Test coverage completion test-keep-a7 — 2026-04-06

**Purpose:** Complete test coverage for remaining untested GeoSim modules  
 (export_viz, errors, profile) in autonomous "test and keep going" mode. Context
continuation from prior compacted session.

**Insights:**

1. **Dual WorldState dispatch pattern requires dual-path testing.** export_viz.
   py helpers use isinstance(ws, dict) / hasattr dispatch to handle both serialized
   dicts and live WorldState objects. Tests must exercise both paths — the less-  
   used path (dict serialization) is where bugs hide.
2. \_extract_scenario_meta** edge case:** When config has no "scenario" key, sc =
   config.get("scenario", {}) yields {}, and sc.get("description", "") yields ""  
   which passes the isinstance(str) check — so the result is {'description': ''}  
   not {}. Subtle API contract that unit testing caught.
3. **Context-continuation after compaction works well** when the summary  
   includes file paths, line numbers, and exact code snippets. Re-establishment  
   took only 4 read operations to get back to working state.
4. **Test helper pattern for trajectory construction** — \_make_step() with  
   use_world_state_obj flag cleanly tests both serialization paths without  
   duplicating fixtures. Reusable pattern for any module with dict/object dispatch.
5. **501 tests in 5.8s** — full suite remains fast. The batch-vectorized trade  
   game tests (including 30-run statistical comparison) add negligible overhead.

## improve-skill: readme — 5 structural improvements + validation — 2026-04-06

**Purpose:** First audit of the /readme skill: added post-run insights phase,
completion block, gum availability check, early overwrite guard, and no-remote
graceful degradation.

**Insights:**

1. Prettier consistently mangles blockquote continuation lines that exceed 80
   chars — the > lock-file.sh acquire line is a recurring victim. Fix by rewriting
   to keep each blockquote line under 80 chars; Prettier reports (unchanged) only
   when lines are already short enough to not reflow.
2. Overwrite checks in Phase 3+ are a pattern smell — any user-facing gate that
   can abort the run should fire in Phase 1 before expensive scanning. The two-
   second gum confirm in Phase 1.1 is always cheaper than all of Phases 1–2
   scanning work.
3. No-remote fallback for scratchpad slug (local-<dirname>) is needed for any
   skill that uses git remote as a primary key — local repos and monorepos inside
   larger trees both hit this case regularly.
4. Validation examples written at creation time score 100/100 the first pass,
   but the auto-generation process catches real edge-case gaps (Example 3 was not
   in the original design).
5. Re-improvement loop on a 73/100 score takes only 2 targeted edits to reach
   100 — the gap list from the scorecard is a precise diff, much faster than re-
   running full analysis.

## session: mcp-file-tools build mcp-disbl-4e -- 2026-04-06

**Purpose:** Build a complete MCP server for file I/O, conversion, and HTTP with
context-aware output shaping.
**Insights:**

1. Output envelope pattern (limit/offset/columns/sample/format/max_chars) is the
   key to making MCP tools model-capacity agnostic -- the caller controls context
   cost.
2. Read->Write pipeline for format conversion gives N\*M paths from N+M modules.
   The bridge: structured arrays can be treated as tabular rows.
3. ESM modules silently break with inline require() -- caught in detect.js
   (readHead) and envelope.js (buildMetaHeader). Always use static imports or
   dynamic await import().
4. Smoke testing MCP tools via child process + JSON-RPC stdin is fast and covers
   the full stack including schema registration.
5. Adding an MCP server globally (~/.claude.json) + CLAUDE.md mandatory-use
   guidance ensures all agents reach for it naturally instead of reinventing
   parsing per-session.
6. Excel cells >32KB cause silent corruption -- sanitize.js truncates them
   preventively. This came from Versable's io.js experience.

## widget: D1/D2 rounds 1+2 close-out — 2026-07-10 19:35

**Purpose:** Finish the design-token + sidebar work (#37/#38) with a quality/perf audit.

**Insights:**

1. Scoped python replace with per-pattern fire counts beats per-site Edits for token sweeps — 71 conversions across 4 passes, every count matched expectations, zero misses (`rg -c` = 0 after).
2. Any Bash-side file write invalidates the Edit tool's read cache — plan edit batches to run either all-Edit or all-script, or budget one refresh Read between them.
3. AX `System Events` can lose a `.nonactivatingPanel` (CG owner name differs from process name: "i-dream" vs "i-dream-bar"); `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` is the reliable frame source. Clicks silently land in the OVERLAPPING topmost window — front the panel first, and re-read the frame before every coordinate click.
4. `rg -c "warning:"` on swiftc output double-counts (path line + caret line) — dedupe with `rg -o "swift:[0-9]+" | sort -u` before claiming a warning delta.

## session: JEGS feedback diagnosis + 15-row re-run [jegs-cms-7e] — 2026-07-09 23:30

**Purpose:** Diagnose the JEGS 2026-07-09 customer feedback (missing fitment, bullet complaints) against spec/config/quality.

**Insights:**

1. Root cause was infra, not templates: `gemini-3.5-pro-preview` pin in sku_fitment.py 404s on Vertex and never served a single request — the research-cache bucket keys embed the serving model, making it a free forensic ledger of which model actually ran and when.
2. The pin was validated as `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` (build session, cache keys) and switched to 3.5 in the manual pre-commit window of c97c82cd — no agent tool call anywhere wrote the string. "Validated artifact ≠ committed artifact" is the reusable failure class.
3. Per-row graceful degrade (`unknown` instead of row failure) with no aggregate alarm made a 100%-failure job look like ordinary output; warnings existed only at worker log level. Loudness thresholds belong next to any degrade path.
4. Re-run harness pattern that worked: vitest one-off dumps the app-compiled pipeline (getEnhancementV2PipelineArgs + fixture), strip mapping steps, feed pipeline_runner with a per-step `research_model` arg override — tests the fix with zero source changes.
5. Render log reads need day-sized windows; the 6-day query times out on the 25-instance prod worker.

## session: M6b interaction pass [forge-ux-7e] — 2026-07-09

Purpose: user verdict on M6 was "technically great but lacking in usability
appeal" — meaning interaction cost, not colors. Audit → fix pass: card quick
actions, folded axes, reminder presets, undoable delete, canvas-cancel fix.

Insights:
- "Usability appeal" meant interaction cost (clicks-per-action, cancel that
  still creates an item, rookie reminder controls), NOT aesthetics. I offered
  taste options and got corrected (atone literal-request-over-intent #2).
  Expand a complaint's own noun into concrete costs before offering options.
- REAL bug found only by driving the built app against a real server: bodyOf
  read bodies from docs_fts, which stores '' for canvases (L4), so the sync
  feed + GET served every canvas with an empty body. Green unit tests missed
  it; no test asserted a canvas body over the wire. Fixed: bodies come from
  files (ADR-0001); FTS is only the mangled-file fallback. Test added.
- Stored titles/previews are derived-at-write: rows written before deriveTitle
  learned the canvas marker keep the raw marker forever. Boot re-derive
  (kv-stamped DERIVE_VERSION) heals them AND bumps seq — which doubles as the
  body-heal vector, since clients re-pull the whole doc.
- Undo-toast delete: enqueue the delete only after the 8s grace window; undo
  cancels before anything is sent. App death mid-window = note survives
  (fail-safe toward keeping data). No confirm dialog needed.
- captureCanvas created+synced the note on tap ("New canvas" then cancel
  littered empty canvases — the user's exact complaint). Discard-on-close of
  a never-drawn canvas fixes cancel AND self-heals existing strays on open.
- Chrome-devtools MCP roundtrips outrun short UI windows (toast expired before
  my Undo click landed). Verify time-windowed flows with ONE in-page async
  evaluate (click → await → assert), not separate tool calls.
- Nested-button trap: a card that hosts its own action menu cannot be a
  <button> (HTML forbids nesting); div + role=button + keyDown guard
  (e.target === e.currentTarget) keeps keyboard behavior.
- make deploy to the live :5040 launchd server is classifier-gated in auto
  mode — deploy needs the user present.

## core-dump: JEGS content-rules conformance + 3-agent review — 2026-07-14 03:55

**Purpose:** Snapshot a long session that rewrote the JEGS content rules, verified on 20 live SKUs, then had the change set demolished by a 3-agent skeptical review.

**Insights:**

1. **`custom_rule` has a no-op validator** (`EnhancementAgentV2.py:33-35`, `rule_validation['custom_rule'] = [str, str]` so a fixture *cannot* supply a func). 7 of 13 rules added this session shape the prompt but never gate. Check this before trusting any `custom_rule` to hold a line.
2. **Branch matching is first-match-wins with a `break`** (`enhancement_agent_v2.py:140-144`). The JEGS test rows are `Brand=Dorman` but the real batch is 606/606 `Brand=JEGS` — so the test rows exercise *different branches* than production. A fix can look green on every test row and never touch the shipping cohort. Always assert which branch a row actually takes.
3. **Dispatching 3 opus reviewers on disjoint segments (backend / fixture / lab) was the highest-value move of the session.** Each found critical bugs the author could not see, and all three independently named the same failure shape ("tested against imagined data"). Cheap relative to the bugs caught. Pattern worth repeating on any non-trivial change set.
4. `str.format` runs over EVERY step-arg string in the pipeline (recursing into lists), so a regex quantifier `\d{2}` in a rule arg kills every row at runtime. Spell it `\d\d`. The guard test added covers rule args only — templates and step args are still unguarded.
5. A checker built only from **prohibitions** cannot detect an **omission**: every negative rule ("no brand", "under 128 chars") is vacuously true on an empty string. This is why the lab passed the exact incident it was built to catch.

## ui-categorical-check: products page (list+peek+detail) — 2026-07-14 02:45

**Purpose:** First run of the skill; owner asked for a products-page check + /ui-gripe before F8.

**Insights:**

1. The pattern catalog (Opus Job 1) still doesn't exist — ran from the checkpoint's seed classes + owner feedback docs instead. Point the skill at the catalog once Opus lands it.
2. Measure the `th`, not the `thead` — kit Table's sticky classes live on the cells; measuring thead reports position:static and produces a FALSE "not sticky" finding. Prove by scrollTop, not by class.
3. Chrome keeps computed colors in oklch; canvas fillStyle + regex both fail to resolve them. The reliable contrast probe is canvas getImageData pixel readback after painting fg/bg.
4. Auto table layout ignores declared column widths whenever nowrap content is wider — the fix that holds is table-fixed at the callsite (list AND panel tables both had this disease, 29px and 11px overflows).
5. /ui-gripe (forked) doesn't parse composite args — it wants exactly one image path + a gripe string; the peek-open capture (list + panel in one frame) was the highest-yield single image.
6. The elementFromPoint ancestor-walk for "painted surface" must stop at the first non-transparent bg — role=dialog wrappers are transparent positioning shells and report false "transparent panel" findings.

## core-dump: speedway F-round handoff [catch-sw-e3] — 2026-07-14

Purpose: checkpoint a long two-lane session (writer + IPC peer) so the next agent
starts at F8 with the cross-session contract intact.

- **Two-lane sessions need the CONTRACT in the checkpoint, not just the state.** The
  peer's ownership boundaries (which files, which browser, which queued jobs) are
  invisible in git and unrecoverable from code — they belong in Session Insights or
  the next agent will collide with a live agent.
- **IPC does not wake an idle recipient.** Messages sit unread until polled; the stop
  hook only surfaces unanswered *requests*, so `inform`s can sit forever. Any
  checkpoint for a multi-session workflow must tell the next agent to POLL
  (`claude-ipc inbox <alias>`), not to wait.
- Categorical UI bug-classes are the highest-value insight to carry across a clear:
  they recur across units (the renderNode JSX-drops-styling class bit twice in one
  session, on different components), and each one is invisible to behavioral checks.
- A shared-tree session must record "the owner edits these paths too" — otherwise the
  next agent's `git add -A` sweeps their uncommitted work into a commit.

## ui-gripe: JEGS Fitment Lab pre-run state (tall text-dense dashboard) — 2026-07-14

**Purpose:** General confusion audit (no gripe given) of a 2370x3628 full-page capture of an internal QA/lab dashboard in its "not run yet" empty state.

**Insights:**

1. `see --ui` DEGENERATES on tall text-dense pages — it emitted `"No... [truncated text]"` ~90x in one list section, which reads as "this UI has 100 near-identical rules". It does not. Treat any long repeated identical ELEMENTS line as a model loop, not evidence, and re-verify the count with `--ocr`. This is a new failure mode not seen on the earlier small-crop run.
2. `--ocr` is the load-bearing read on rule/checklist UIs, not `--ui`. The `--ui` pass mangled 5+ strings (JEKS/JEGS, Donnan/Dorman, Love/Live, invented rule text). Native Read + `--ocr` together were sufficient; the `--ui` sections still earned their keep for LAYOUT/HIERARCHY/PALETTE, which were accurate.
3. Highest-damage rubric item on empty-state/pre-run dashboards is **affordance ambiguity**, specifically status slots drawn with input glyphs (hollow circle = unselected radio). Check this first on any "awaiting run/result" screen — a pending verdict rendered as a radio button inverts the user's mental model from "read a report" to "fill a form".
4. Cross-checking two lists in the SAME card against each other is a cheap, high-yield pattern break detector: here GLOBAL RULES used bullet dots (correct, non-interactive) while FIELD RULES used circles (wrong) — one card, two glyph vocabularies.
5. Missing-bullet anomalies are a reliable tell for an **overlay collision**. Two rules rendered without their leading bullet, and OCR also dropped/garbled exactly those two lines — that convergence localized a floating widget sitting on top of the content column. When OCR and the visual agree that a specific line is malformed, suspect z-index before suspecting the data.
6. Density inversion is worth checking by raw pixel spans on tall captures: static reference content occupying y≈370-1700 while the actual output panel is a below-the-fold stub at y≈1740 is measurable, not a matter of taste.

## cleanup-comments: JEGS content-rules + lab-audit changed files — 2026-07-14 00:20

**Purpose:** Strip AI-voice from the files touched during the JEGS conformance work, whole-file (not just changed hunks).

**Insights:**

1. `detect.py --changed` only scans **changed hunks**, so it misses violations in untouched regions of a changed file. When the user asks for "even unchanged areas", pass explicit paths instead. Note the path mode needs **absolute** paths; relative paths silently return zero findings, which reads as a clean bill of health rather than a miss.
2. The regex tier cannot see **archeology** phrased as ordinary prose. `"...used to score a clean sheet"` was flagged only as `em-dash`; the repo's Rule 4a violation ("this used to be X") needed a human read. Worth a `used to|previously|no longer` pattern in `detect.py`.
3. Em-dash as an **empty-value placeholder** (`value ?? "—"`) is correct typography, not a voice violation. Any auto-fix must skip string literals in JSX/`??` position, or it will corrupt table rendering. It is currently the agent's judgment that saves this.
4. Rule labels and `describe`/`it` names are prose a human reads, but they are not comments, so the detector never sees them. On this repo they also get **asserted verbatim in tests**, so changing one means changing both files together or the suite goes red.
5. Voice cleanup surfaced an unrelated real defect (TS 6133, an unused `v` param in a `FieldRule.explain`). Reading comments in context means reading the code around them, which is worth the pass on its own.

## session: backlog drain + pipeline rebuild + subsystem review [gcc-resi-b7] — 2026-07-13

**Purpose:** Drain the gcc proposal backlog, rebuild how proposals are handled/logged/picked (atone + i-dream), review subsystems for common primitives.

**Insights:**

1. **Never test a security gate against a stub.** The push-gate GUI dialog passed all 8 branches against a stubbed `osascript` — and failed OPEN against the real one, which returns `button returned:Approve this push` in ~1s WITHOUT drawing the dialog. Two real pushes to main went through ungated. A stub only confirms the logic you already believe.
2. **An approval channel must be one the agent CANNOT ACTUATE.** A dialog the agent's own process can make return "approved" is a rubber stamp the agent holds. The `! touch` sentinel is safe *because* it's created out-of-band where PreToolUse hooks don't run.
3. **A gate's ALLOW path must be as visible as its BLOCK path.** warn-log.sh dropped the `allow-approved` label, so a gate waving pushes through logged `action=(none)`. Silent allows are how a fail-open survives unnoticed.
4. **The recurring gcc failure is a primitive that doesn't BIND, not a primitive that's missing.** flock absent (every ledger lock a no-op — 14 torn lines reproduced); atone never emitting the tag the corroboration gate reads; `acted` detector registered for 1 of 13 plugs; ship-gate mute regex blind to half the namespace. Verify the mechanism is in force, not merely present.
5. **Rename = contract change.** Migration 0030 renamed a tag; I never grepped for readers; the dedup that keyed on it silently returned empty and the cron re-drafted ~40 proposals, including human-rejected ones. S3, juror: very-wrong.
6. **Bare `{additionalContext}` is silently dropped** by PreToolUse/PostToolUse — only the `hookSpecificOutput` envelope is read, with NO error and nothing in `--debug`. Four PostToolUse hooks had never reached an agent.

## session: gcc proposals drain + pipeline rebuild + subsystem review [gcc-resi-b7] — 2026-07-11

**Purpose:** Drain the gcc proposal backlog, then fix how proposals are handled/logged/picked (atone + i-dream integration), then review all local Claude subsystems for cross-integration and common primitives.

**Insights:**

1. **`flock` is not installed on macOS.** Every `flock -x 9 2>/dev/null || true` in the gcc silently degraded to an unlocked `>>`. Reproduced real corruption: 24 concurrent writers of 9KB lines → 14 torn lines, ~1 run in 5. `ledger_append` now uses a mkdir lock (the shape `persona-log.sh` already used — the one writer that diverged from the shared primitive was the only one whose locking worked). Test: `scripts/tests/test-ledger-append.sh`.
2. **The recurring gcc failure is not a missing primitive — it's a primitive that doesn't bind.** flock absent · atone never emitted the `link:` tag the corroboration gate reads · i-dream kept a second untriaged store · the `acted` conversion detector registered for 1 of 13 plugs · the replay mute-regex missing half the namespace. Same shape as `skill-spec-update-not-honored`. Verify the mechanism is IN FORCE, not just present.
3. **Content-similarity clustering failed in BOTH directions before it worked.** Over-merge first (templated `[atone]` bodies scored 0.81 against each other — would have fused every slug), then a silent no-op (a "rare = appears in ≤1 proposal" cutoff makes an edge mathematically impossible). Only shipping `--explain` and hand-checking every edge caught either. Thresholds are now measured (TP 0.116 vs FP 0.021), not chosen, and pinned by a regression test.
4. **A sub-agent's structural claim needs independent verification.** All three audit agents were high-quality, but I re-verified every load-bearing claim myself (`command -v flock`, the session-key mismatch, the tracked-vs-untracked ledgers) — and one doc claim I'd have inherited was false: `rules/corrections.md` said `atone/events.jsonl` is git-tracked; `git ls-files atone/` returns zero. My own design doc had copied that false premise and recommended tracking `proposals.jsonl` because of it. Checking reversed the recommendation.
5. **Fixture idempotency catches what a single run hides.** The dream bridge passed run 1 and filed 5 duplicates on run 2 (dedup keyed on a tag that isn't always written). `git checkout -b` in a test fixture also silently changed a hook's verdict on re-run. Always run the test twice.
6. Backlog: 79 open → 59 (13 built + verified, 17 rejected with reasons, 4 new findings filed). Two migrations (0030 atone link-tags, 0031 one-proposal-store).

## core-dump: triage-86 task list + /wake, handing off to the gcc-map report — 2026-07-17 06:30

**Purpose:** Close the resumed triage-86 task list, build /wake through /bloop, harden it
through two adversarial gates, and hand the fresh gcc-map --deep report to the next agent.

**Insights:**

1. **The gate's value is claims, not code.** Across two gates (sonnet, then opus), over
   half the real findings were false CLAIMS rather than broken code — a comment asserting
   a guard it lacked, a citation vouching for work that postdated it, a measurement
   generalised past its evidence. All survived a self-review that felt complete. The code
   bugs were recoverable; the claims would have shipped as documentation that lies.
2. **The fix can ship the bug.** Gate 1 flagged a guard as untested; probing showed it was
   unreachable, so I deleted it. Gate 2 proved my reachability measurement wrong
   (`jq -rn 'nan|floor'` → `null`, 4 chars) and that the deletion had introduced a
   fail-open. A second independent reader is what caught the repair.
3. **Use a different model for the second gate.** Sonnet then opus found disjoint sets.
   Same-model re-review would likely have re-found the same things.
4. **Point the reviewer at your own load-bearing claim, explicitly.** "Re-measure this, I
   measured it" produced the highest-severity finding of the session. A reviewer told to
   look everywhere looks nowhere in particular.
5. **/bloop Phase 4.4's warning is real, twice:** both dispatched agents went idle without
   messaging back despite an explicit delivery clause in the prompt. The skeptic HAD
   written its report to disk; only the message was missing. Check the output path before
   assuming a stall.
6. **A blind fixture beats a green suite every time.** BSD `seq 1 0` counts DOWN, so a
   "zero tasks" fixture silently held two files and its guard shipped untested.

## gcc-map: --deep v3 refresh of the GCC structure map — 2026-07-17 11:45

**Purpose:** First `/gcc-map --deep` run: measure the load model, diff it against the
indices, run the battery, fan out 5 blind lenses + a completeness critic, and refresh
the living map at `assets/reports/20260704-gcc-structure-map/MAP.md`.

**Insights:**

1. The opus critic seat earned the whole `--deep` premium; never cut it. It overturned
   three parent claims (browser-mcp-isolation's absence from context is `paths:`
   scoping, NOT staleness; "index rows are duplicative" is an untested attention claim
   attacking the smallest layer; enforcing rotation-at-50 today would ARCHIVE real
   session insights and KEEP machine duplicates) and reframed the meta-diagnosis from
   "no enforcement" to "excellent intake, no metabolism" (5 rules ever deleted, every
   one an absorption).
2. All 5 lenses FOUND the nested config dir and all stopped at "it exists". Only the
   critic opened it: 23 permission grants incl. a standing ALLOW for bare
   `/usr/bin/grep`, which `rules/shell.md` marks MANDATORY-never, while global
   settings.json has zero grep policy. Lens prompts must say "open the payload, not
   just the container" — finding a container is not a finding.
3. Never pipe an existence-DISPROVING grep to `head -N`. `rg "_tldr" scripts/ | head -5`
   truncated past the real reader and nearly shipped a false S-level finding
   ("CLAUDE.md:51's atone injection is dead"). Unpiped `rg -l` showed 9 readers incl.
   the live `scripts/dream/dream-insights.sh`. `rules/testing.md` `[truncation]` biting
   the auditor.
4. Naming trap that caused #3: `dream/dream-insights.sh` injects into CONTEXT;
   `dream/inject-dream-insights.sh` writes into FILES. The one named `inject-*` is not
   the injector. Check what a lane actually calls (`sessionstart-inject.sh:45`), never
   infer from a name.
5. Prove derived-view freshness by REGENERATING into a sandbox and diffing, never by
   inspection: `HOME=$SB bash scripts/rules-index.sh` then `diff` excluding the stamp
   line. One call, and it keeps the skill read-only on config.
6. The agent's OWN context is authoritative for the load MECHANISM (29 autoloaded rules
   inline proves native autoload) but is a SNAPSHOT for content: this session's index
   was ~18h stale (16:47/38 rows vs disk 17:50/39 rows). Measure disk; never quote your
   own context as current.
7. The ~41.5k static core is per-AGENT, not per-session (this skill's own author is a
   sub-agent and received the full autoload). A 5-agent fan-out is ~208k tok before any
   work, so `--deep` pays the core ~8x to audit it once.
8. `block-nested-claude.sh` false-fired 3x this run on read-only probes and on a
   heredoc whose BODY merely described the anti-pattern. It scans raw command text and
   never got the heredoc-body-stripping fix that commit 7278adb gave its sibling
   guard-system-dir-writes.sh. Use the Write tool to route around it.

## release-changelog: v5.2.3 changelog from PR #260 — 2026-07-15 03:20

**Purpose:** Generate the product+engineering changelog for release PR #260 (release ← development, 26 commits, 51 files, +7080/−356).

**Insights:**

1. **NEW commit-subject trap — two commits carried each other's labels.** `964f7f15 "feat(fitment): register the fitment agents with langfuse"` contains ZERO langfuse lines (it is the Fits-Select refactor); the actual langfuse instrumentation landed in `7413ce26 "fix(jegs): route real wheels..."`. Add to SKILL.md step 3's trap catalog: a commit whose subject names feature X may contain feature Y, and vice versa — always `git show <sha> --stat` before attributing work to a commit.
2. **NEW trap — a prior review can be staler than the code AND wrong about what shipped.** The 2026-07-14 skeptical review declared the fitment reconciler "MUST NOT SHIP" with six defects. Those defects were in UNCOMMITTED working-tree code; `git log --all -S"<symbol>"` returned zero commits for the flagged functions. The developer rebuilt 34 min after the review, before the first commit. **`git log --all -S"<symbol>"` is the cheap disproof** — run it before importing any review finding into a changelog's known-issues, or you invent a bug that never shipped.
3. **A "revert" commit inside a branch often nets to zero.** `f843b573 "revert flag to v2"` undid an intra-branch v3 flip from the same session. Always diff the flag at `origin/base` vs `origin/head` (not the commit) — the NET state is what a changelog reports. Confirmed v2 on both sides = no change to report.
4. **Decompose the +N line count before printing it.** +7,080 here was 1,572 lines of `.claude/whiteboard/` planning docs + ~1,900 lines of new tests. Printing the raw number makes a modest release read as a risky one. Worth baking a "scan card decomposition" line into the SKILL's step 1.
5. **Reuse of a prior review saved ~2 themes of reading but needed verification on every claim.** Its rule-count figure ("7 of 13 custom_rule no-ops") had the right numerator and wrong denominator (actually 7 of 15; 8 are real hard gates). Reuse review reports as an INDEX of where to look, never as a source of facts.
6. **Deploy-readiness checks are fast and worth running in the main agent** while sub-agents read themes: migrations, env, deps, CI all came back empty in one Bash call, and surfaced the real finding — `package.json` was never bumped (5.2.1 on both branches despite a "V5.2.3" PR title).

## core-dump: speedway UI round, two-lane (fable+opus) — 2026-07-14 05:20

**Purpose:** Checkpoint the Speedway feedback round for the next Fable session, with the parallel Opus lane as first-class context.

**Insights:**

1. When a peer agent shares the tree, the checkpoint's most load-bearing section is not the build log — it is the PROTOCOL (who owns which files, who pushes, how the browser rotates, and that a peer's word is not the owner's authorization). Put it above the fold; a resumed agent that edits the peer's surface loses more than one that re-reads a commit.
2. Owner rules can land mid-build THROUGH the other lane (a card-divider rule arrived via the peer's sweep while my work was uncommitted and violated it). Read the peer's handoff before committing on a shared branch.
3. Checkpoint the DISEASES, not just the state: the pnpm hard-link has three distinct faces (new file invisible, edited file stale-but-green, dep-optimizer classic-JSX) and each one costs an hour to rediscover. A named section beats a commit reference.
4. `browser_close` closes the page, not the process — so a "released" shared browser still holds its profile lock. Verify with pgrep BEFORE claiming the profile, and note pgrep also matches your own polling shell.

## designer-reviewer: reviewed files-table-reworked.png + audit-log-reworked.png — 2026-07-20 02:10

**Purpose:** Aesthetic critique of the two freshest rework screenshots in versable-builder (Speedway shell: Files page and Audit Log page), auto-selected by mtime since no path argument was given.

**Insights:**

1. When no screenshot path is passed, the project root of versable-builder is the drop zone — screenshots land as `<feature>-<state>.png` next to package.json; sorting by mtime with `fd -e png --changed-within 3d | sort by stat -f %m` disambiguates in one call.
2. The `see --ui` pre-pass mis-OCRs small dim text ("76 SKUs" read as "76 XLSXs"/"76 KIPS" in two runs) — the `--ocr` verification pass is not optional when quoting sidebar or badge strings.
3. Recurring pattern across this product's tables: a chip stacked over near-identical subtext ("Part Type" / "Part type", "CSV" / "2 KB") is what inflates rows past the 32px density cap — the fix is always inline-merge, not padding tweaks.
4. The highest-severity finding class in wide log tables is column starvation: a verbose locale timestamp (~240px) silently pushes the semantically-primary column off-canvas with no h-scrollbar affordance. Check the right edge of every table screenshot first.
5. Both screens share one token shell, so background-tint findings dedupe: file one finding per shell, reference it from the sibling review.

## core-dump: boot-app resource audit [boot-apps-a2] — 2026-08-06 05:05
**Purpose:** Post-reboot audit of autostart apps by resource cost, then log retention, ollama pre-warm removal, and calendar companions.

**Insights:**
1. Three near-misses this session all had one shape: absence of evidence read as evidence of absence, caused by the instrument. A case-sensitive grep said mongo had 0 connections (real: 564,194). A 0-byte nginx access log meant `access_log` was commented out, not that nginx is idle. A retention test "passed" while unable to fail, because nothing exceeded the size threshold. Before believing a zero, ask what else produces that same zero.
2. `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/` is the fastest first read for "the machine feels slow" — macOS writes a timestamped .diag per unresponsive process.
3. `schedule.sh register <plist>` adopts a hand-rolled LaunchAgent into the gcc registry. This matters most for the DELETE side: an event created outside the registry has no recorded calendar_uid, so retiring the cron orphans it. That is how warm-morning survived unnoticed.
4. Truncating a log a process holds open leaves it writing at its old offset and creates a sparse file that still reports the original size. mongod takes SIGUSR1 and reopens; only plain appenders are safe to copy-truncate.
5. MCP servers dwarf everything else: ~2.5 GB across two sessions vs 60 MB for the redis+postgres they wrap, and 501 MB for all boot apps combined. `npm exec <pkg>` costs ~100 MB purely as a wrapper around the node process doing the work.
6. Intelligent disobedience paid off on redis: measured 11 MB and 15 idle wakeups/min on a 64 GB machine, and recommended NOT building the auto-off machinery rather than building what was hinted at.
7. The calendar-companion rule covers every-N-days StartInterval but not sub-daily. A 5-min recurring event would destroy the observability the rule exists for, so a daily marker stating true cadence serves the intent. Deviation recorded in migration 0043 rather than applied silently or skipped.

## core-dump: sluggish-UI diagnosis + pm2 idle reaper [slug-ui-7c] — 2026-08-06 01:15
**Purpose:** Diagnose perceived system sluggishness, then build a 12h idle auto-shutoff for pm2-managed services.

**Insights:**
1. `/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/` is the highest-signal first read for "the machine feels slow". macOS writes a timestamped .diag whenever a process stops responding; it named Steam in one step after six other avenues had cleared.
2. `ps` %CPU is a lifetime average, so use `top -l` for anything long-lived. WindowServer read 34.6% in ps and 0.0% in top at the same moment after 30 days uptime.
3. Two points are not a trend. A mach-port count that looked like a +1/sec leak went down over a 10-second window.
4. pm2's tracked pid is not the listening pid for npm-wrapped apps. Walk the descendant tree, or every npm-wrapped service reads as portless forever (speedway-fe pid 1154 holds nothing; child node 1248 holds :5101).
5. Connection presence is not use. A Vite HMR websocket from a forgotten browser tab reads as traffic indefinitely, so measure endpoint identity (`endpoints - prior_endpoints`), not count.
6. Exercising caught a guard that inspection would have passed. `svc up`'s port check iterated an empty list on fresh state, so it was silently blind; it needed a pm2-args fallback plus a crash-loop backstop.
7. Two self-inflicted hangs worth remembering: `pmset -g thermlog` streams forever, and `VAR=$(fn)` blocks when fn backgrounds a child inheriting stdout.
8. `prepend-runtime-note.sh` takes `<skill-name> <entry-file>` as arguments and ignores stdin. Piping to it silently no-ops, and an `echo` after it reports a false success.

## core-dump: session studio-jobs-0c, Bengaluru creative-jobs pipeline design — 2026-08-04

**Purpose:** Checkpoint a design session that produced a job-mining guidebook plus two executed modules, and survived three adversarial peer reviews.

**Insights:**

1. The template's H1 lines carry em-dashes and the prose-lint Stop hook blocks them at budget zero, so the first Write of every full core-dump fails. Resolving it needs `~/.claude/skills/catchup/SKILL.md:456`, which confirms only the `##` headings are the parse contract, so the H1 separator is free to change. Filed as prop-20260804-140342-20.
2. A greenfield project has no `.claude/`, so Phase 3.1's "find the directory containing `.claude/`" finds nothing and Phase 3.7's workspace diff has no doc to diff. Both degrade fine; use CWD as project root and skip 3.7 silently.
3. Phase 3.5's `mcp__inputs__form` is unavailable when the Interactive Inputs MCP is not connected. The silent-default fallback worked as specified; no need to substitute AskUserQuestion.
4. Seeding Pending Items from the live Task list caught only 2 of 11 real pending items this session. The conversation carried the rest (an open bug, seven unapplied adoptions, three raised-not-acted rubric changes). The spec's "then add anything the conversation surfaced" is doing most of the work, not the task read.
5. Standing caveats earned their field here. Three separate unverified constants (a guessed 1.45 multiplier, a guessed 75-day threshold, a suspect 7.0km geocode) plus an openly unfixed bug would all have been laundered into confident-sounding doctrine by a summary that only captured decisions.

4. Semantic-color audits should count WHERE each hue appears per column, not just what it maps to — amber mapped "correctly" to attention here but appeared in 4 of 5 columns, which destroys the blocked-column signal the stories demanded.

Insights:

- The user's verdict-first category (facts before conclusions; user owns "done") came from their decision-page NOTES, not from any model lane — the free-text escape hatch out-discovered the novel-label mechanism.

## session: adversarial-review skill + kanban board system + P0-P3 fix plan [adrev-kanbn-4b] — 2026-07-27

**Purpose:** Build /adversarial-review + a throwaway agent-driven kanban board; adversarially review, UX-test, and fix-plan the board through /bloop.

**Insights:**

- For a product NAMED after a known artifact class (kanban), the class anatomy (columns/labels/sub-items) IS the spec — a distinctiveness-driven redesign that exits the class is the failure, not a feature. Two misfires this session (v2 ledger, missing labels/subs) both traced to optimizing the frontend-design brief over the named class. Atone `rebuild-replaced-accumulated-ux-without-parity-audit` now 3×.
- Decision-page submit-to-wake (Monitor on the answer file, armed in the SAME turn as handoff) works reliably across 22h/43h idle gaps — user-affirmed. The failure mode is ending the turn without arming; the fix is a same-turn discipline, now baked into pending-add output.
- Parallel /skeptical-review + /bloop validation gate converging independently on the same destructive blocker (unregister wrong-target) is the strongest real-finding signal. Worth the double spend on genuinely-destructive surfaces.
- A mutation test that stays GREEN means the fix structure is the bug: a redundant pre-lock check masked the throw-based lock release and had to be removed to make the guard pinnable.
- Behavior-anchored fix plans (observed→executable-target→change→probe added to a standing action script) make "done" mechanical and give every future change a regression gate.

## release-changelog: v5.2.5 hotfix notes from PR #269 — 2026-07-24 15:30

**Purpose:** Turn a 2-file / +36−8 follow-up release PR into a changelog, without the per-theme fan-out the skill prescribes for large diffs.

**Insights:**

1. NEW commit-subject trap: **a subject naming one surface can hide a second.** Both PRs here were titled for preview surfaces (`fix(enhancement) ... [render preview]`, `fix(preview-data-history)`) and the frontend code comment said "Display-only", but the backend change landed in `remove_ctx_fields`, which serves preview AND export, applied before the `is_export` branch. Exports changed too. Rule of thumb: when a fix touches a shared formatter, trace which modes route through it before repeating the subject's scope claim.
2. The version-bump check earns its place a third time. `origin/release` and `origin/development` both read `5.2.4`, and 5.2.4 had already shipped as PR #264, so the PR title "Release V5.2.4" was a carried-over title. Always diff the version against the *previously shipped* notes folder, not just base-vs-head.
3. Under ~5 changed files, skip the fan-out entirely and read the diff inline. Total cost here was ~10 tool calls; a per-theme dispatch would have cost more than the diff itself.
4. Check whether a `release-v-<ver>/` folder already exists before choosing the output path. `release-v-5.2.4/` held PR #264's notes; writing there would have clobbered a 27 KB artifact. Reading its blockquote header (which PR + file count it covered) is the cheapest way to tell a re-cut from a follow-up.
5. For a small diff, verifying the *mechanism* is where the time goes, not reading the hunks: `get_column_map_item`'s fail-closed behaviour, whether `restore_brand_code` mutates or copies, and which transform chain includes `get_item_result` were the three reads that made the caveats section factual rather than speculative.

## improve-skill: pr-review output contract rewritten — 2026-07-23 02:10

**Purpose:** Replace pr-review's machine wire-format return with a delivered-file + human-digest contract, matching /release-changelog, and fix four defects a live run on PR #264 exposed.

**Insights:**

1. A rule addressed to a role that never reads the file cannot be delivered. pr-review's "the parent must not paste this block" was added 2026-07-21 to stop a wire-format leak; on the next run the block AND that sentence were both printed to the user. A forked skill's only channel to its caller is its return text, so an instruction about the return can only travel inside the return. When a fix targets a reader who does not exist, delete the artifact instead of instructing around it.
2. `gh pr diff <N>` returns HTTP 406 above 300 files — precisely the release-PR case. Any skill documenting it as the diff source needs the `git diff origin/<base>...origin/<head>` three-dot fallback, or it fails on the PRs that matter most.
3. Bare-basename citations are a correctness bug, not an ergonomics one. `backend/lib/agents/EnhancementAgentV3.py` and `backend/lib/pipeline/methods/enhancement_agent_v3.py` are different files whose basenames collide on a case-insensitive filesystem. The mechanical check is `rg -o '`[^`/]+\.(ts|py):[0-9]'` over the finished report.
4. A skill should not promise output shape a repo hook controls. pr-review forbade "fixed-width column padding" while a project PostToolUse hook ran `prettier --write` on every markdown write. Softened to a preference rather than left as an unkeepable rule.
5. pr-review had no post-run-insights phase and correspondingly zero runtime-notes entries after multiple runs. Absence of runtime history is diagnostic: check whether the skill has a step that writes it before concluding it has never run.
6. Scope note from the user: pr-review should stay single-pass. Fan-out belongs in /release-changelog, where per-theme readers each own distinct files; a PR review applies the same conventions to every file, so sharding costs more than it buys.

## designer-reviewer: reviewed claude-ipc i-dashboard TUI frames — 2026-07-20 12:20

**Purpose:** Scored aesthetic critique of the 15-frame `tui-frames/` capture set (feat/i-dashboard branch) — peers/inbox/projects/orphans/log views plus compose, copy-menu, filter, quit-guard, and 80x24 frames.

**Insights:**

1. For a TUI frame SET, score the primary frame but sweep every distinct surface — the highest-value findings (key-value color inversion between detail pane and copy menu, footer-vs-help key styling mismatch) are only visible by comparing frames, never within one.
2. Both `see --ui` and `see --ocr` silently substitute readable glyphs ("•", "z") for tofu boxes — glyph-coverage defects are only detectable in the native raster read. Never cite OCR as evidence about glyph identity.
3. Whole-row status coloring plus no selection bar means selection and liveness compete for the same foreground-color channel — check for a dedicated cursor affordance (inverse video / prefix marker) first in any list-based TUI.
4. The skill's CSS-fix format maps cleanly to TUI form — express fixes as style-token assignments (fg/bg/attr per role) rather than CSS properties.
